clue.text: Person deceived but not downhearted

annotationWithheld.why: Person deceived but not downhearted (4): DUPED less a D would need 'not down', but 'downhearted' gives no D by any convention and nothing else explains the word; the clue looks misprinted

clue.text: Rectifying infernal world husbandry

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, the infernal realm
husbandry is farming, and tilling is working the soil

explanation.surface: Someone sets right the farming practices of hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rectifying' is used in its chemistry sense: to rectify a spirit is to purify it by repeated distillation.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, rectifying a liquid means purifying it by distilling it again and again.

clue.text: Shop around for peat substitute in Holyhead, and fertilizer

indicators.note: turned around, so the four letters of shop are rearranged
one piece is put inside the other
a substitute version of peat, so its letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the head of holy, its first letter

explanation.surface: A gardener in the Welsh port of Holyhead hunts the shops for a peat replacement and some plant food.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'head' of Holyhead is H, the first letter of holy; Holyhead is a ferry port in Wales. 'around' and 'substitute' each rearrange their word, and 'in' sets H within the shuffled peat.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosphates are mineral salts spread on fields as plant food.

clue.text: Expert history teacher?

parts.note: history is what is past
a schoolmaster is a teacher

explanation.surface: Is the best person for the job a history teacher?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal split: a teacher of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A past master is someone thoroughly skilled at something, an adept.

clue.text: Insect reaching elephant's tail from another beast

indicators.note: the tail of the word elephant is its closing letters, here the final three

parts.note: the word supplies its closing letters
the lion is a second beast besides the elephant

explanation.surface: A bug manages to reach an elephant's tail starting from another big animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' here means the closing stretch of the word elephant, not just its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The antlion is a winged insect whose larvae dig pits to trap ants.

clue.text: Hairstyle not up to certain standard

annotationWithheld.why: Hairstyle not up to certain standard (7): rev(NOT) + SURE (certain) gives TONSURE, but 'standard' does no job in any reading, so the clue as held looks garbled
annotationWithheld.clue: Hairstyle not up to certain standard

clue.text: Blind men stayed in circulation, behaving like some professors

indicators.note: circulating, the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Sightless men stay moving about, acting like dreamy academics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in circulation' tells you to rearrange all fourteen letters of BLIND MEN STAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: The absent-minded professor is a stock figure, forgetful and lost in thought.

clue.text: Runs in the first heat?

parts.note: reads like a sprinter in a qualifying race, but means ice and snow that melt and run when the first warm weather comes

explanation.surface: An athlete competes in the opening round of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: When snow melts in early warmth it turns to running water.

clue.text: Charge for a plant

explanation.surface: A fee is levied for one shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge is to dash at speed; the second sense is a grasslike marsh plant used for weaving.

clue.text: Poker-faced, despite fast moving lioness in angry pursuit

parts.note: an express is a fast-moving train or service

indicators.note: chasing in anger, the letters of lioness run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a straight face though a lioness charges after them in fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast moving' together gives EXPRESS; 'in angry pursuit' turns LIONESS into IONLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker player keeps a blank face that shows no feeling.

clue.text: With them on the warpath, the number holding out tails off

indicators.note: the number wraps round the next piece

parts.note: six is a number

indicators.note: the word out loses its tail, its last letter

explanation.surface: A warning about warriors: a figure stays outside while tailing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tails off' trims the last letter of OUT, and 'holding' puts the remainder inside the number. The definition is a whole phrase: the people with whom one went 'on the warpath' in Westerns.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sioux were Plains peoples famed in Westerns for going to war against settlers.

clue.text: The cask belongs to a Scotsman? Other folk!

parts.note: a tun is a large cask
the cask is his: 'is' plus a possessive
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a typical Scotsman's name; IAN'S is his

explanation.surface: Is that barrel a Scot's? No, it belongs to foreigners!
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'The cask is Ian's': TUN IS IAN'S, a Scotsman owning it.
explanation.definitionFit: People of a North African country are, to a Briton, another nation altogether.

clue.text: Deaf to argument? Presume vision's faulty

definitions.note: the definition is an adjectival phrase for a noun answer: the quality of being deaf to argument

indicators.note: a faulty arrangement, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with poor eyesight takes for granted what others argue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' tells you to rearrange the fourteen letters of PRESUME VISION'S; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unmoved by any reasoning is a closed, unpersuadable mind.

clue.text: Carriers spreading germs around the place in Germany

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the next piece
germs spread, so their letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr

explanation.surface: Disease carriers spread infection around a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' scatters GERMS as M...GERS, which 'around' wraps about the German city, so the rearranged letters split either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Messengers carry letters and news from one person to another.

clue.text: Union trouble about relative entertained

annotationWithheld.why: Union trouble about relative entertained (7): rev(AIL) + SON gives only LIASON; nothing supplies the second I and 'entertained' has no piece to take in, so the clue as held is short of a word

clue.text: Let me return to get the wahoo

annotationWithheld.why: Let me return to get the wahoo (7): the only parse is LET ME + RE rearranged by 'turn', so 'return' would give RE and also be the anagram signal, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Let me return to get the wahoo

clue.text: Quiet roads-by deploying them?

indicators.note: deploying sends forces out into position, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the printed words, read with one E fewer as quit roads, are the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Streets fall silent once police in protective gear are sent out.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's fodder has one E too many; the anagram works with QUIT ROADS, nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Police trained for disorder are sent out to clear and calm the streets.

clue.text: Dire suffering-first born in greater extremity

indicators.note: the born piece is placed at the front

parts.note: née, French for born, marks a maiden name

indicators.note: suffering knocks the letters of dire into disorder

explanation.surface: A newborn arrives first in terrible distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges DIRE, and 'first' brings the word for born to the front although the clue gives it last. Née is French for born, used before a maiden name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone more in want is poorer and in worse straits.

clue.text: Gross iniquity of holding captive the musician

indicators.note: the two words hold the musician inside them, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A great wrong is done by keeping a composer prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was an Italian composer of operas such as The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Chap tries to get fruit

parts.note: a chap is a man
goes, as in 'has a go', means tries

explanation.surface: A fellow makes efforts to obtain something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: These are tropical stone fruits with sweet orange flesh.

clue.text: Low gear change needed for parking by the bank

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: a change of order, so gear is rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver must drop to a low gear before pulling in next to the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective for the gear; it is a cow's call, MOO. 'change' turns GEAR into RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring place for a boat at the riverside is where it is parked.

clue.text: Won't sit down to talk the matter over

definitions.text: Won't sit down to talk the matter over

parts.words: Won't sit down to talk the matter over
parts.note: reads as a refusal to negotiate, but literally describes someone on their feet in order to argue a point

explanation.surface: A stubborn party refuses to join talks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means something is obvious and logical; the clue takes its words literally as remaining upright to argue.

clue.text: Top job in the building industry

definitions.text: Top job in the building industry

parts.words: Top job in the building industry
parts.note: sounds like the chief post in construction, but means work on the top of a house, laying its roof

explanation.surface: Someone holds the most senior position in construction.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofer laying slates works at the very top of a building.

clue.text: Come up against objection

explanation.surface: Someone meets resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To border on is to touch at the edge; split as 'a but', it is a single protest.

clue.text: All brain and energy, this lady?

definitions.text: All brain and energy, this lady?

indicators.note: she is a dancer who spins, so the letters spin too into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Is this woman nothing but intellect and vigour?
explanation.walkthrough: No word says rearrange outright: the whirling dancer implied by 'this lady?' spins ALL BRAIN plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer in classical ballet needs both discipline and stamina.

clue.text: Look to employ this despicable creature

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in 'lo and behold'
to employ is to use

explanation.surface: Watch how you deal with this vile animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasitic insect, and figuratively a contemptible person.

clue.text: Revolvers at the entrance

parts.note: suggests armed guards with pistols at the door, but means rotating barriers

explanation.surface: Gunmen are posted at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating gates admit one person at a time to a ground or station.

clue.text: Does wrong, gets lines

definitions.note: plural lines of verse for plural poems

indicators.note: done wrong, so the letters fall into a different order

explanation.surface: A doe goes astray and is punished with lines to write.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems are written in lines of verse.
